o1.biggest_strength: It turns the two biggest signals in the data into the launch strategy: creator/author-led acquisition and a staged existing-user rollout gated by hotkey and extension migration health.
o1.biggest_mistake: The channel table says it is ranked by users kept but is really prioritised by retention quality and strategic upside, so the ranking logic needs one clarifying sentence.

o2.biggest_mistake: The launch assets are not ready to use because they contain placeholders, and the plan sends Show HN, all-user email, creator posts and X on launch day despite saying the rollout is staged.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove placeholders, align the staged rollout with the email and channel timing, and move Hacker News/Product Hunt into a lower-priority reach phase after migration is stable.

reason: Output 1 is much closer to a launch plan we could run: it has dated owners, real gates, finished copy, and it protects the hotkey/extensions promise. Output 2 has useful thinking, but it needs too much cleanup before the team could trust or ship it.
